courses.title: Foundations of Information Technology
courses.description: An introduction to foundational concepts in information technology including hardware, software, networks, and data management.

courses.title: Foundations of Networking
courses.description: Introduction to computer networks, data communications, OSI and TCP/IP models, architectures, and networking standards.

courses.title: Foundations of Cybersecurity
courses.description: Fundamental security principles, threats, attacks, defenses, authentication, cryptography, and risk assessment.

courses.title: Network and Cloud Security
courses.description: Exploration of security issues in modern computer networks and cloud environments, including firewalls, IDS/IPS, and security postures.
courses.prereq_display: ICS 21400 AND ICS 31000 AND IIT 22000 AND MTH 14100

courses.title: Digital Forensics and Cyber Investigation
courses.description: Techniques for computer crime investigation, forensic imaging, file system analysis, digital evidence handling, and legal compliance.

courses.title: Linux Server Installation & Configuration
courses.description: Installation, configuration, maintenance, security hardening, and scripting in enterprise Linux operating systems.
courses.prereq_display: ICS 21300 AND MTH 14100 AND (IIT 22000 OR CSC 35500)

courses.title: Cloud Computing Essentials and Best Practices
courses.description: Cloud service models, infrastructure deployment, security paradigms, resource management, and best practice architectures.

courses.title: Hybrid Cloud Architecture and Management
courses.description: Designing, integrating, maintaining, and automating hybrid cloud architectures across on-premises and multi-cloud providers.

courses.title: Ethical Hacking
courses.description: Methodologies and tools used by penetration testers to identify, exploit, and remediate system and network vulnerabilities ethically.

courses.title: Advanced Penetration Testing
courses.description: Deep-dive offensive testing against modern operating systems, web applications, and network infrastructures with red-teaming techniques.

courses.title: Cybersecurity Analysis
courses.description: Threat hunting, behavioral analysis, Security Operations Center (SOC) operations, and log correlation techniques.

courses.title: Secure Software Development
courses.description: Application security concepts, OWASP Top 10 defenses, secure code review, and development lifecycle security integrations.
courses.prereq_display: ICS 31000 AND MTH 14100 AND (IIT 21500 OR CSC 10011 OR CSC 24400)

courses.title: Web Based Application Security
courses.description: Assessing and defending web-based applications, client-server security protocols, injection flaws, and web services protection.

courses.title: Cybersecurity Capstone
courses.description: Comprehensive integration project demonstrating cybersecurity mastery, incident handling, defense posture design, and reporting.
courses.prereq_display: Senior Status (90+ credits) and Last Full Semester

courses.title: Programming Logic and Design
courses.description: Fundamental programming structures, logic development, pseudocode, flowcharting, modular design, and control structures.
courses.prereq_display: ICS 21300 AND (MTH 11000 OR MTH 14100+ OR Math Placement)

courses.title: Hardware and Operating Systems
courses.description: Personal computer hardware architecture, storage systems, device configuration, installation, and operating system management.

courses.title: Ethical Issues in Cybersecurity
courses.description: Ethical, legal, societal, and regulatory dilemmas facing cybersecurity practitioners, data privacy frameworks, and professional codes.

courses.title: Blockchain Technology for Business
courses.description: Decentralized ledgers, smart contracts, cryptographic consensus algorithms, token economics, and enterprise blockchain deployments.

courses.title: Database Analysis and Design Concepts
courses.description: Relational database concepts, entity-relationship modeling, normalization, SQL queries, DDL, DML, and database administration.

courses.title: Project Management in Information Technology
courses.description: Project lifecycle, scope management, scheduling, risk estimation, agile and waterfall methodologies in technology initiatives.

courses.title: Agile Software Development
courses.description: Agile methodologies, Scrum, sprint planning, user stories, continuous delivery, and collaborative software engineering.

courses.title: Mobile Applications Programming
courses.description: Mobile application development lifecycle, UI widgets, responsive layouts, data persistence, and cross-platform tooling.

courses.title: C# Programming
courses.description: Object-oriented programming using C# and .NET framework, class structures, interfaces, LINQ, and modern software design patterns.

courses.title: Fundamentals of HTML
courses.description: Modern semantic HTML5, CSS3 styling, responsive web layouts, accessibility standards, and document structuring.

courses.title: Applications in Web Development
courses.description: Front-end and back-end integration, client-side scripting with JavaScript, DOM manipulation, asynchronous requests, and web APIs.

courses.title: Systems Analysis and Design
courses.description: Software development life cycle, requirement modeling, UML diagrams, architectural patterns, feasibility, and implementation planning.

courses.title: Database Application Implementation
courses.description: Advanced database application design, stored procedures, triggers, ORMs, and application database connectivity. Offered strictly in Summer.
pe_notes: Forced Summer Exception: Offered in Summer only

courses.title: Fundamentals of User Interface Design
courses.description: User experience (UX) and user interface (UI) principles, human-computer interaction, wireframing, prototyping, and accessibility.

courses.title: Applications in Object-Oriented Web Development
courses.description: Server-side web development using modern object-oriented languages, MVC architecture, sessions, and web service consumption.

courses.title: Applications in Multi-Tiered Web Programming
courses.description: Multi-tier application architecture, business logic tier separation, persistent storage layers, and secure distributed communications.

courses.title: Information Technology Capstone
courses.description: Culminating team or individual software/systems implementation project integrating degree skills with comprehensive documentation and review.
courses.prereq_display: Senior Status (90+ credits) and Last Full Semester

courses.title: Cisco I-Introduction to Networks
courses.description: Architecture, structure, functions, components, and models of the Internet and computer networks. Cisco CCNA preparation lecture.
pe_notes: Cisco Concurrent Lab Exemption Rule applies

courses.title: Introduction to Networks Lab
courses.description: Hands-on laboratory configuration of switches, routers, IP addressing, and cabling corresponding to ICS 32300.
pe_notes: Must take concurrently with ICS 32300 unless exempt

courses.title: Cisco II-Routing and Switching Essentials
courses.description: Architecture, components, and operations of routers and switches in a small network. VLANs, dynamic routing, and ACLs.
pe_notes: Cisco Concurrent Lab Exemption Rule applies

courses.title: Routing and Switching Lab
courses.description: Hands-on laboratory configuration of dynamic routing protocols, VLANs, trunking, and access control lists.
pe_notes: Must take concurrently with ICS 32400 unless exempt

courses.title: Cisco III-Scaling Networks
courses.description: Architecture, components, and operations of routers and switches in larger, complex networks. OSPF, EIGRP, STP, and EtherChannel.
pe_notes: Cisco Concurrent Lab Exemption Rule applies

courses.title: Scaling Networks Lab
courses.description: Hands-on laboratory configuration of enterprise campus topologies, hierarchical routing, link aggregation, and network monitoring.
pe_notes: Must take concurrently with ICS 32500 unless exempt

courses.title: Network Management
courses.description: Network monitoring tools, SNMP, automation scripts, performance baseline auditing, fault tolerance, and disaster planning.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Data Center Virtualization
courses.description: Hypervisor technologies, virtual storage networks, ESXi, cluster resource management, virtual network switches, and high availability.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Cloud Computing
courses.description: Public, private, and hybrid cloud architectures, virtualization infrastructures, cloud service models, and virtual data centers.

courses.title: Cloud Computing Concepts (Legacy)
courses.description: Legacy cloud computing coursework, direct replacement course is ICS 41500.
pe_notes: Legacy course replaced by ICS 41500

courses.title: Cloud Architecture (Legacy)
courses.description: Legacy cloud architecture coursework, direct replacement course is ICS 41700.
pe_notes: Legacy course replaced by ICS 41700

courses.title: Intermediate Algebra
courses.description: Linear and quadratic equations, inequalities, graphs, polynomials, and rational expressions.

courses.title: Basic Statistics (GE-Math)
courses.description: Descriptive statistics, elementary probability, normal distribution, sampling distributions, hypothesis testing, and confidence intervals.
pe_notes: Dual-satisfies GE-Math and Major Math requirements

courses.title: College Algebra (GE-Math)
courses.description: Functions and graphs, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic functions, systems of equations.

courses.title: Precalculus: Elementary Functions (GE-Math)
courses.description: Trigonometric functions, identities, inverse trigonometric functions, and analytic trigonometry.

courses.title: Calculus I (GE-Math)
courses.description: Limits, derivatives, applications of differentiation, antiderivatives, and definite integrals.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: Integration techniques, applications of definite integrals, infinite sequences and series, parametric equations, and polar coordinates.

courses.title: Introduction to Programming
courses.description: Introductory programming concepts, algorithm development, control structures, and basic object orientation.

courses.title: Programming in Python
courses.description: Python programming syntax, data structures, modules, file I/O, object-oriented concepts, and basic scripting.

courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Processes, threads, CPU scheduling, synchronization, deadlocks, memory management, and file systems.

courses.title: Information Security
courses.description: Cryptographic tools, user authentication, access control, database security, malware, and intrusion detection.

courses.title: Composition I (GE-Comm)
courses.description: College writing emphasizing critical reading, rhetorical analysis, drafting, revision, and analytical composition.
courses.prereq_display: Grade of C or higher required to satisfy Composition I
pe_notes: Gatekeeper: Grade of C or higher required

courses.title: Composition I - English for Academic Purposes (GE-Comm)
courses.description: Academic composition tailored for international and English-language learners.
courses.prereq_display: Grade of C or higher required to satisfy Composition I
pe_notes: Gatekeeper: Grade of C or higher required

courses.title: Composition II (GE-Comm)
courses.description: Advanced argumentative writing, academic research methodologies, source synthesis, and documentation.
courses.prereq_display: ENGL 15000 or EPP 15000 with grade of C or higher
pe_notes: Gatekeeper: Grade of C or higher required

courses.title: First-Year Experience
courses.description: Introduction to collegiate success, academic resources, community engagement, and intellectual growth.

pe_notes: Waived for transfer students with TR > 0

courses.title: U.S. History to 1877 (GE-HC: USHisGov)
courses.description: Survey of political, economic, cultural, and social developments of the United States from colonial origins through Reconstruction.

courses.title: American National Government (GE-HC: USHisGov / GE-Civ)
courses.description: Constitutional foundations, federalism, branches of government, civil liberties, interest groups, and political behavior.

courses.title: Principles of Psychology (GE-SocSci)
courses.description: Survey of psychology including biological bases of behavior, sensation, perception, learning, cognition, development, and social psychology.

courses.title: Basic Concepts of Sociology (GE-SocSci / HD)
courses.description: Sociological perspectives on social structure, culture, stratification, race, gender, institutions, and social change. Carries Human Diversity (/HD).
pe_notes: Carries Human Diversity (/HD) attribute

courses.title: Concepts in Biology with Lab (GE-NatSciLec/Lab)
courses.description: General biology for non-majors exploring cellular biology, genetics, evolution, diversity, and ecology with integrated lab.

courses.title: Physical Geology with Lab (GE-NatSciLec/Lab)
courses.description: Earth materials, plate tectonics, geological hazards, minerals, rocks, erosion, and planetary processes with integrated lab.

courses.title: Art Appreciation (GE-Human Culture: Art)
courses.description: Visual arts appreciation covering aesthetic elements, artistic media, art history, and critical analysis of major art works.

courses.title: Introduction to Theatre (GE-Human Culture: Art)
courses.description: Theatrical arts, dramatic literature, playwriting, performance, directing, stage design, and historical theatrical styles.

courses.title: World Literature I (GE-Human Culture: Literature)
courses.description: Masterpieces of world literature from antiquity through the Renaissance in cultural and historical context.

courses.title: African American Literature (GE-Human Culture: Literature / HD)
courses.description: Survey of African American literature from slave narratives through the Harlem Renaissance to contemporary writers. Carries Human Diversity (/HD).
pe_notes: Carries Human Diversity (/HD) attribute

courses.title: World Religions (GE-HC / HD)
courses.description: Comparative study of world religions including Hinduism, Buddhism, Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Carries Human Diversity (/HD).
pe_notes: Carries Human Diversity (/HD) attribute

courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy (GE-HC)
courses.description: Introduction to major philosophical questions: epistemology, metaphysics, ethics, political philosophy, and logic.

courses.title: Cultural Anthropology (GE-HC / HD)
courses.description: Comparative study of human cultures, kinship, religion, linguistics, economic systems, and cultural change. Carries Human Diversity (/HD).
pe_notes: Carries Human Diversity (/HD) attribute

courses.title: GE: Composition I (3cr)
courses.description: General Education requirement in written communication (Composition I). Requires a grade of C or higher in ENGL 15000 (Composition I) or EPP 15000 (Composition I - English for Academic Purposes).

courses.title: General Education: Composition II
courses.description: General Education requirement in advanced research and argumentation (Composition II). Requires a grade of C or higher in ENGL 17000 (Research and Argumentation).

courses.title: GE: Mathematics (3cr)
courses.description: General Education requirement in mathematical reasoning. Fulfills 3 credits of quantitative analysis. Satisfied by MTH 14100 Basic Statistics, which dual-satisfies the Major Math requirement, or by any approved GE-Math course (MTH 15100+).

courses.title: General Education: U.S. History / Government
courses.description: General Education requirement in American history or national government. Recommended options: HIST 10500 (U.S. History to 1877), HIST 10600 (U.S. History since 1877), or PS 15500 (American National Government).

courses.title: General Education: Social Science
courses.description: General Education requirement in social sciences. Recommended options: PSY 10000 (Principles of Psychology), SOC 10200 (Basic Concepts of Sociology /HD), ANT 11200, ECON 23010, or ECON 23020.

courses.title: General Education: Natural Science with Lab
courses.description: General Education requirement in natural science with laboratory component (4 credits). Recommended options: BSC 10000 (Concepts in Biology with Lab), ESC 10000 (Physical Geology with Lab), CHM 10000, or PHY 10000.

courses.title: General Education: Science Elective
courses.description: General Education elective satisfied by any additional course in social sciences or natural sciences (PSY, SOC, ECON, ANT, BSC, ESC, CHM, PHY, SCI).

courses.title: General Education: Fine Arts
courses.description: General Education requirement in Human Culture: Arts. Fulfills 3 credits of creative and aesthetic inquiry. Recommended options: ART 18100 (Art Appreciation), TA 11700 (Introduction to Theatre), MUS 10000 (Music Appreciation), or DAN 10100.

courses.title: General Education: Literature
courses.description: General Education requirement in Human Culture: Literature. Recommended options: ENGL 20100 (World Literature I), ENGL 20200 (World Literature II), or ENGL 21600 (African American Literature /HD).

courses.title: General Education: Human Culture I (Non-Literature, Non-Arts)
courses.description: General Education requirement in Human Culture excluding Literature and Arts. Recommended areas: World History, Religion (REL 20000 /HD), Philosophy (PHL 10000), or Foreign Languages and Cultures (SPA, FRN).

courses.title: General Education: Human Culture II
courses.description: Secondary General Education requirement in Human Culture. Any remaining course carrying the GE-HC attribute across History, Philosophy, Religion, Arts, Literature, or Foreign Language.

courses.title: General Education: Elective I
courses.description: General Education elective chosen from any approved course carrying a General Education attribute across departments.

courses.title: General Education: Elective II
courses.description: Secondary General Education elective chosen from any approved course carrying a General Education attribute across departments.

courses.title: General Elective
courses.description: General elective credits required to meet the 120-credit minimum threshold for bachelor degree completion.

courses.title: Upper-Level Elective (30000+)
courses.description: Upper-division elective course numbered 30000 or higher, required to satisfy the university policy requiring at least 42 upper-level credit hours.
